prompt:
You are a financial analyst reviewing a company's annual report for the fiscal year ending March 2022.
Today's date is April 2022 — you have JUST received the FY2022 annual report and must forecast ahead.

CRITICAL RULES:
1. Do NOT use your training knowledge about actual results after FY2022.
2. Treat FY2022 as the MOST RECENT year you know about. Any data in the text for years after 2022 must be IGNORED.
3. Your forecast must be derived solely from data up to and including FY2022.

Step 1: From the consolidated P&L statement, find Revenues (the reported top-line revenue figure —
        use the SAME line item consistently across all years) and Net Income (PAT) for the years
        shown up to FY2022.
Step 2: Calculate the year-on-year growth rates using only data up to FY2022.
Step 3: Use the FY2022 growth rate as your primary projection assumption.
Step 4: Project Revenue and Net Income forward for FY2023, 2024, 2025 only.
Step 5: Estimate EPS = Net Income / shares outstanding.
Step 6: Set "base_year" to exactly 2022 in your JSON response.
BANKS/NBFCs: use "Total Income" (Interest Earned + Other Income) as Revenues — banks have no Revenue from Operations line.

RESPONSE FORMAT: Begin your response DIRECTLY with the opening brace { of the JSON. Do NOT write any reasoning, steps, or explanation before the JSON — put your reasoning inside the "reasoning" field instead.

UNITS RULE: Express ALL monetary values in plain INR Crores (e.g., 853000 for ₹8.53 lakh crore).
Never use thousands of crores, lakh crores, millions, or billions.

Step 7: Return ONLY valid JSON — no prose, no explanation outside the JSON:
{
  "strategy": "baseline",
  "base_year": 2022,
  "forecast": [
    {"year": <YYYY>, "revenue_cr": <number>, "net_income_cr": <number>, "eps": <number>},
    ...
  ],
  "reasoning": "<2-3 sentences on growth rate assumptions>"
}

Recovery Rates Recovery rates reflect the estimated loss that the company will suffer given expected defaults (Non-performing Assets). The recovery rate is given as a percentage and reflects the opposite of loss severity (i.e. 100% recovery reflects 0% loss severity). In line with the operation of the Company, probability of Non-performing assets to loss assets plays an important role to ascertain the recovery rates. Higher loss severity levels / lower recovery rates indicate lower expected cash flows upon the default of the instruments. Recovery rates for complex, less liquid instruments are usually unobservable and are estimated based on historical data. Revenue from operations Revenue is the value of all sales of goods and services recognized by a company in a period. Revenue (also referred to as Sales, Turnover, or Income) forms the beginning of a company’s Income Statement and often considered the “Top Line” of a business. Growth in revenue from operation directly impacts the profitability of the company, as operation expenses are deducted from a company’s revenue to arrive at its profit. 36.11. De-recognition An item of Property, Plant and Equipment and any significant part initially recognized is de-recognized upon disposal or when no future economic benefits are expected from its use or disposal. Intangible assets An intangible asset is recognized only when its cost can be measured reliably and it is probable that the expected future economic benefits that are attributable to it will flow to the Company. Leases (a) Company as a lessee (i) The Company recognizes a right-of-use asset and a lease liability at the lease commencement date. The right- of-use asset is initially measured at cost, which comprises the initial amount of lease liability adjusted for any lease payments made at or before the commencement date, plus any initial direct cost incurred and an estimate of costs to dismantle and remove the underlying asset or to restore the underlying asset or the site on which it is located, less any lease incentives received. (ii) The right-of-use asset is subsequently depreciated using the straight-line method from the commencement date to the earlier of the end of the useful life of the right-to-use asset or the end of the lease term. The estimated useful life of the right-to-use asset is determined on the same basis as those of property, plant and equipment. In addition, the right-to-use asset is periodically reduced by impairment losses, if any, and adjusted for certain re-measurements of the lease liability. (iii) The lease liability is initially measured at the present value of the lease payments that are not paid at the commencement date, discounted using the interest rate implicit in the lease or, if that rate cannot be readily determined, the Company’s incremental borrowing rate.
